links.outcome: Whether EMR-only follow-up data can validate model discrimination and calibration versus registry-plus-EMR reference standard
links.effect: C-index 0.67 (EMR only) vs 0.66 (reference); IBS 0.16 vs 0.17; performance drops tracked similarly with fewer features. EMR-only data wrongly showed systematic survival underprediction (calibration).
links.quote: EMR data were useful for validation of model discrimination, but not calibration.

links.outcome: Whether EMR-only outcome data can estimate real-world model accuracy compared with higher-quality ground truth
links.effect: Discrimination estimates with EMR data matched the reference standard (C-index 0.67 vs 0.66), but calibration was misjudged: EMR-only data showed underprediction of survival while the reference showed reasonable calibration.
links.quote: When using reference standard data, the model was found to be reasonably calibrated, but with EMR data, the model was incorrectly found to systematically underpredict survival.
